# Overview

SACAT analyzes microbiome counts to separate evidence for differences in
structural absence (SA) from differences in relative abundance conditional
on presence (RA). Sequencing depth enters the model because a zero can
reflect either absence or nondetection. RA effects are standardized over
covariates and centered against a reference from other eligible taxa.
The primary omnibus p-value is `min(1, 2 * min(p_SA, p_RA))`.
Benjamini–Hochberg (BH) adjustment is applied separately to each result family.

# Installation

Install SACAT from GitHub using R 4.6.0 or later and a C++ compiler.

```{r installation, eval=FALSE}
install.packages(c("BiocManager", "remotes"))
BiocManager::install("Statwright/SACAT")
```

```{r packages}
library(SACAT)
library(SummarizedExperiment)
```

# Prepare the data

The bundled `skin_microbiome` data contain 16S counts and metadata from
58 unrelated participants in Potbhare et al. (2022), prepared from the
`mia` dataset `peerj13075`. We compare the recorded mixed (`Mixed`) and
vegetarian (`Veg`) diet groups, adjusting for gender, age group, and location.

```{r example-data}
data("skin_microbiome", package = "SACAT")
counts_all <- skin_microbiome$counts
metadata <- skin_microbiome$metadata
dim(counts_all)
table(metadata$Diet)
```

Counts must be nonnegative integers, with taxa in rows and samples in
columns. Metadata row names must match sample names. Use complete values for
the binary group and adjustment variables. The formula requires an additive
group effect; group interactions, offsets, and random effects are unsupported.

The bundled library sizes are totals from the full released count table.
Preserve them when selecting taxa. For your own data, retain the original
sequencing depths and supply raw counts without pseudocounts or normalization.

```{r full-library-sizes}
full_depth <- colSums(counts_all)
stopifnot(
    identical(colnames(counts_all), rownames(metadata)),
    all(metadata$library_size == full_depth)
)
```

Select the 20 taxa detected in the most samples, breaking ties by name.
These taxa define the feature set for this example's tests and abundance
reference.

```{r select-features}
selected <- order(-rowSums(counts_all > 0), rownames(counts_all))[seq_len(20L)]
se <- SummarizedExperiment(
    assays = list(counts = counts_all[selected, , drop = FALSE]),
    colData = metadata
)
se
```

# Fit and inspect the results

`sacat_se()` extracts the count assay and `colData()` from the container.
Set `reference = "Veg"` for a mixed-minus-vegetarian comparison. This call
fits both components using the default numerical settings and retains plot
data. `sacat(counts, metadata, ...)` provides the equivalent matrix interface.

```{r fit-model}
fit <- sacat_se(
    se,
    formula = ~ Gender + Age + Geographical_location + Diet,
    group = "Diet",
    reference = "Veg",
    library_size = "library_size",
    assay = "counts",
    store_plot_data = TRUE
)
fit
```

```{r primary-results}
result_columns <- c(
    "taxon", "p_adj_structural_absence", "p_adj_relative_abundance",
    "p_adj_omnibus", "estimate_relative_abundance"
)
knitr::kable(fit$results[, result_columns], digits = 4, row.names = FALSE)
```

Positive SA statistics indicate greater absence in the comparison group.
Positive RA estimates indicate a present-conditional log-abundance contrast
above the cross-taxon reference. The omnibus result combines component
evidence; inspect the separate SA and RA columns to interpret an association.

Retained taxa with an unavailable component receive an operational p-value
of one in that family. Taxa excluded by the initial positive-count filter
have missing results. Diagnostics explain component availability and warnings:

```{r component-diagnostics}
diagnostic_columns <- c(
    "taxon", "reason_structural_absence", "reason_relative_abundance"
)
knitr::kable(head(fit$diagnostics[, diagnostic_columns]), row.names = FALSE)
```

# Plot the association profile

Show three taxa with available fitted profiles. The plot uses the summaries
stored in the fitted object.

```{r association-profile, dev="svg", fig.width=11, fig.height=5.5, out.width="100%", fig.cap="SACAT profile for three taxa. BH adjustment uses the full retained tutorial feature set."}
profiles <- fit$plot_data$profiles
shown <- profiles$feature[profiles$structural_status == "ok" &
                          profiles$abundance_status == "ok"]
plot(fit, features = head(shown, 3L),
     group_labels = c("Vegetarian", "Mixed diet"))
```

**A: Component evidence.** Signed SA and RA statistics; filled markers
indicate component discoveries. BH boundaries use the complete retained
families, and taxon superscripts summarize omnibus adjusted p-values.

**B: Detection and zero sources.** Observed detection and model-estimated
SA and nondetection (ND) shares sum to one in each group. The zero-source
shares average posterior probabilities over all samples in the observed
group, using a descriptive structural fit with group and covariate effects.

**C: Abundance.** Positive observed counts divided by full library sizes,
expressed as percentages on a log scale. Diamonds show exponentiated mean
fitted log relative abundance conditional on presence, standardized over all
covariate profiles. The raw abundance contrast is the natural log of the ratio
of the comparison-group diamond to the reference-group diamond. The RA test
subtracts the estimated cross-taxon reference from this contrast.

See `?sacat`, `?sacat_se`, and `?plot.sacat` for all arguments. Request
`full_output = TRUE` for detailed fits and additional numerical diagnostics.

# References and session information

Potbhare R, RaviKumar A, Munukka E, Lahti L, and Ashma R (2022). Skin microbiota
diversity among genetically unrelated individuals of Indian origin.
*PeerJ* **10**, e13075. [doi:10.7717/peerj.13075](https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj.13075).
The count table is [Supplemental Information 1](https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj.13075/supp-1).
The article and supplements are published under
[CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/).
The [mia dataset documentation](https://microbiome.github.io/mia/reference/peerj13075.html)
and `?skin_microbiome` describe the data and its preparation.

```{r session-info}
session <- sessionInfo()
for (field in intersect(c("BLAS", "LAPACK"), names(session))) {
    session[[field]] <- basename(session[[field]])
}
print(session)
```
